# Architecture, generated from the source

<!-- Generated by tools/make_architecture_doc.py. Do not edit by hand: change the code or the generator and run `python tools/make_architecture_doc.py`. tests/test_architecture_doc.py fails when this file is out of date. -->

> Hand-written: the framework designs and runs ELM experiments. Reception and the Planner are language-model agents that design a study; code checks the design; the model server (`mcp/elm-mcp`) owns what is known about ELM, builds the runs and computes their numbers; the numbers report and the Analyzer read those records. Everything below this note is read from the code except the `FLOW` list in section 6 (the order of the stages, their titles and the functions named for each), which is hand-written and marked so there. The page drawn by `tools/make_arch_map.py` is the same picture with hand-written detail, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the top of the repository is the hand-written overview.

## 1. Components that call a language model

A component is listed when one of its functions calls a model (`.ask(...)` or `...completions.create(...)`) or constructs a model client. The client itself is in section 2. "Called from" lists the framework functions outside the module whose calls reach a model through it, and then any code under `mcp/` (a server's own script) that does.

## 2. The language-model endpoint and client

Every construction of a model SDK client in framework code, with the endpoint it is given and the environment variable its key is read from (the variable's name only).

| where | function | SDK client | endpoint | key read from | default model id |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/agents/llm_agent.py` | `SimpleLLMClient.__init__` | `openai.OpenAI` | `https://ai-incubator-api.pnnl.gov` | `PNNL_API_KEY` | `"claude-opus-4-8-project"` |

The classes in `src/agents/llm_agent.py`:

- `SimpleLLMClient`: Wrapper around OpenAI client for PNNL API.
- `LLMAgent`: Simple LLM-based agent.

The reply limit (`max_tokens`) at each model call in framework code, as the code sets it:

- `src/agents/analyzer_agent.py::AnalyzerAgent._chat`: 1200 (`max_tokens`, the default of `AnalyzerAgent._chat(max_tokens)`); `AnalyzerAgent.interpret` passes `1600`
- `src/agents/analyzer_agent.py::AnalyzerAgent.review_figure`: 400
- `src/agents/llm_agent.py::SimpleLLMClient.ask`: 16384 (`self.max_tokens`, set in `SimpleLLMClient.__init__`)
- `src/agents/tool_loop.py::ToolLoopAgent._create`: 8192 (`self.max_tokens`, the default of `ToolLoopAgent.__init__(max_tokens)`)

## 3. MCP servers and the tools they serve

The registry the framework reads is `mcp_config.template.json` (copied to the git-ignored `mcp_config.json` on each machine). A tool's callers are the framework functions that name it as a whole string literal, bare or as `server__tool`, in their body or in a module or class constant they use (a constant no function uses is credited to its module), and the prompts that name it. A tool with no caller may still be reached by a language model choosing it from a server's tool list.

### `ameriflux`

Registry description: AmeriFlux eddy-covariance towers: ET comparison sites. Discovery is open; downloading series needs AMERIFLUX_USER_ID and AMERIFLUX_EMAIL.

Entry: `mcp/ameriflux-mcp/main.py`, 4 tools.

| tool | what it does (its docstring's first line, or its description's first sentence) | called from |
|---|---|---|
| `get_et` | AmeriFlux eddy-covariance towers in a bbox; the ET validation source. | `src/core/data_gather.py::gather_observations` |
| `data_status` | Can this server fetch flux SERIES right now, and if not, what is missing? | no framework caller |
| `request_flux_data` | Submit the AmeriFlux download request for these sites. NEEDS CREDENTIALS. | no framework caller |
| `describe_ameriflux_capabilities` | What this server can and cannot answer. Read before planning with it. | `src/core/model_servers.py::_describe_tool_name (by the pattern _DESCRIBE)` |

### `daymet`

Registry description: Daymet V4 daily 1 km weather from ORNL DAAC. Free and keyless. Note it returns HTTP 200 and the whole archive for an out-of-range year, and its calendar is always 365 days.

Entry: `mcp/daymet-mcp/main.py`, 3 tools.

| tool | what it does (its docstring's first line, or its description's first sentence) | called from |
|---|---|---|
| `describe_daymet_capabilities` | What this server provides, the years it holds, and whether it is reachable. | `src/core/model_servers.py::_describe_tool_name (by the pattern _DESCRIBE)` |
| `get_precipitation` | Daily Daymet series at ONE point (1 km, North America). | no framework caller |
| `get_precipitation_points` | The same for MANY points in ONE MCP session; use this whenever you have more than one location, e.g. forcing a set of sampled columns. | `src/core/data_gather.py::gather_precipitation` |

### `elm`

Registry description: E3SM Land Model, 1-D columns: builds and submits CIME cases. Needs an E3SM source tree, a scratch filesystem and a working sbatch; no web credentials. The long timeout is deliberate, since a case build is slow.

Entry: `mcp/elm-mcp/main.py`, 22 tools.

| tool | what it does (its docstring's first line, or its description's first sentence) | called from |
|---|---|---|
| `describe_elm_capabilities` | What this server can do, what it needs, and whether that is present. | `src/core/model_servers.py::_describe_tool_name (by the pattern _DESCRIBE)` |
| `build_elm_inputs_from_location` | Turn sampled column locations into everything ELM needs to run them. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._refine_columns` |
| `set_initial_water_table` | Write an initial water table into a single-column ELM finidat. | no framework caller |
| `describe_conceptual_factors` | What a controlled ELM sweep can vary, and what it cannot. | `src/core/sweep_menu.py::fetch` |
| `check_conceptual_design` | Will this sweep do what it looks like it does? Ask before spending compute. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_sweep_columns`, `mcp/pflotran-mcp/pflotran_exp_manager.py::PFLOTRANExpManager._build_sweep_columns` |
| `build_conceptual_columns` | Turn a checked sweep into the same columns.json a sampled run produces. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_sweep_columns`, `mcp/pflotran-mcp/pflotran_exp_manager.py::PFLOTRANExpManager._build_sweep_columns` |
| `get_column_metadata` | The FINAL columns; post warm start, with the soil their grid cells supplied. | no framework caller |
| `run_elm_ensemble` | Build the cases and run every column, as ONE job. Returns its id. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_cases` |
| `build_elm_cases` | Compile the CIME cases. SUBMITS a job and returns its id. | no framework caller |
| `extract_elm_output` | Every column's daily series, out of the history files and onto disk. | no framework caller |
| `compare_to_obs` | Model against observations for this study. MEASUREMENTS ONLY. | no framework caller |
| `check_elm_job` | What is SLURM doing with this job? Works for build and run alike. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._poll` |
| `read_domain_recipe` | The recipe of an existing CIME case, read from the case's own records. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_case`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._control_recipe`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager.preview_design` |
| `check_domain_inputs` | Do this surface, domain and saved state make one input set ELM will run? | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_case`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_experiment` |
| `write_domain_case` | Write the case script, the stage script and the job plan. Submits nothing. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager.preview_design` |
| `submit_domain_chain` | Check the input set, write the scripts and submit the chain. JOB IDS. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._submit_domain`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._submit_experiment` |
| `check_domain_chain` | Where a whole-domain chain stands: each stage's SLURM state and check verdict. `active` is the field to branch on (true while a stage may still run; a stage SLURM no longer knows, or one an earlier failure stopped, has ended and says so under `inferred`); `failed_stage` names the first stage that ended without passing; `years_passed` the model years whose check passed; `chain_ok` that every stage ended and passed. `ok` says only that the question could be answered. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._poll_domain`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._poll_experiment` |
| `describe_domain_controls` | The prepared whole-domain controls this machine has, and their facts. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_experiment`, `src/agents/prompts/reception_agentic.txt (prompt)`, `src/agents/reception_llm.py::LLMReceptionAgent.__init__`, `src/agents/reception_llm.py::LLMReceptionAgent._control_card`, `src/core/model_servers.py::describe_domain`, `src/core/model_servers.py::model_tools` |
| `refresh_domain_control_facts` | Read one prepared control's facts from its own output, and cache them. | no framework caller |
| `describe_domain_changes` | What a whole-domain experiment may change in its control. THE MENU. | `src/agents/prompts/reception_agentic.txt (prompt)`, `src/core/model_servers.py::describe_domain`, `src/core/model_servers.py::model_tools` |
| `check_domain_experiment` | Will this experiment do what it looks like it does? Ask before any job. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_experiment` |
| `build_domain_runs` | Each run's recipe, chain spec and checks, from the experiment. Submits nothing. | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_experiment` |

### `pflotran`

Registry description: PFLOTRAN: variably-saturated flow and reactive transport. NOT in this repository. It is a console script installed from the separate repo reaction_sandbox_mcp (branch compy-port), so this entry is dead until that is pip-installed into your environment. The console script takes no arguments, so args is an empty list; it must still be present.

Entry: the command `pflotran-mcp`. Its arguments name no server file in this repository, so its tools are not read here.

## 4. Where framework code reaches a server without MCP

Framework code that loads a module from a server's directory in its own process instead of calling one of the server's tools: each function that loads a module from a file path (`spec_from_file_location`) where the path or the caller is under `mcp/`, and each import of a module that lives only under `mcp/` from outside that module's directory. The reason is quoted from the code: the function's docstring, the comments that speak of loading by path, in-process or MCP, and the comments just above the loading statement.

| loader or importer | what it loads | the reason the code gives |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_coupled_columns` | `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( "compare_pflotran", pkg / "__init__.py", submodule_search_locations=[str(pkg)])`<br>where `pkg = framework_dir() / "mcp" / "pflotran-mcp" / "compare"` | The prior PFLOTRAN run's columns, each carrying its next start. compare/water_table.solved_water_table_m, loaded by path from beside the PFLOTRAN server; the meaning of that model's output stays on that model's side. the one function that owns "where PFLOTRAN's water table IS". Resolved through the framework, not by counting parents, so this still points at the sibling server when elm-mcp is checked out on its own. |
| `src/agents/analysis/step1_compare.py::_load_compare` | `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( name, pkg / "__init__.py", submodule_search_locations=[str(pkg)])`, with `_SERVER_SRC = { "elm": _ROOT / "mcp" / "elm-mcp" / "src", "pflotran": _ROOT / "mcp" / "pflotran-mcp", }` | The model's comparison package, imported once under `compare_<model>`. IN-PROCESS RATHER THAN OVER MCP, deliberately. The Analyzer must run against an ARCHIVED run directory with no servers configured; that is what makes step 3 re-runnable, and it is how this step is developed. A tool call would make the Analyzer's one input a live subprocess. LOADED BY PATH UNDER A UNIQUE NAME. Both packages are called `compare`, so the old "append the server dir and __import__('compare')" would hand a PFLOTRAN run whichever package a previous import had cached. Each is loaded from its own __init__.py as `compare_<model>`; relative imports inside the package resolve against that name. |
| `src/core/exp_manager_base.py::ExperimentManagerBase._sibling_module` | `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._attach_runs` loads `mcp/elm-mcp/src/domain_case.py` (uses `CHAIN_FILE`, `chain_records`)<br>`mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_case` loads `mcp/elm-mcp/src/domain_case.py` (uses BESIDE this manager, under a per-model name, so two servers' same-named modules do not collide. Loaded by path under `{name}_{MODEL}`, the same way step1_compare loads each model's compare package. |
| `src/core/resumable.py::_manager_for` | imports `PFLOTRANExpManager` from `pflotran_exp_manager` (`mcp/pflotran-mcp/pflotran_exp_manager.py`) | The manager class for a backend name, or None if there is not one. BOTH MANAGERS LIVE BESIDE THEIR SERVER, under mcp/<server>-mcp/, and are imported by path: src/core/ names no model (ELM moved 2026-08-10, PFLOTRAN 2026-08-18). A new model adds one branch here. |
| `src/core/resumable.py::_manager_for` | imports `ELMExpManager` from `elm_exp_manager` (`mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py`) | The manager class for a backend name, or None if there is not one. BOTH MANAGERS LIVE BESIDE THEIR SERVER, under mcp/<server>-mcp/, and are imported by path: src/core/ names no model (ELM moved 2026-08-10, PFLOTRAN 2026-08-18). A new model adds one branch here. |

## 5. Third-party libraries

## 6. The whole-domain flow

> Hand-written: the order of the stages, their titles and the functions named for each (`FLOW` in the generator; every function is checked to exist). Read from those functions: whether a language model is reached (with one call path to it), the MCP tools they name, and the records they read and write, counting the functions they call (two calls deep) in the same directory. Records are found by the rules in the generator's notes (a file name written in the code, or a constant bound to one, inside a reading or writing call), so `none` means none found by those rules; a name built at run time is not seen.

1. **Reception reads the request, asks the person, gathers the place**
   - code: `src/agents/reception_llm.py::LLMReceptionAgent.__init__`, `src/agents/reception_llm.py::LLMReceptionAgent.process`, `workflow.py::_save_reception`
   - language model: yes, `LLMReceptionAgent.process` -> `LLMReceptionAgent._ask_for_the_json` -> `ToolLoopAgent._create`
   - MCP tools named: `describe_domain_controls`, `get_elevation`, `resolve_watershed`
   - reads: `columns.json`, `conus2_subsurface.json`, `reception.json`
   - writes: `conus2_subsurface.json`, `reception.json`, `reception_brief.json`
2. **The Planner designs the experiment against the server's rulebook**
   - code: `workflow.py::WorkflowCoordinator._plan`, `workflow.py::WorkflowCoordinator._domain_rulebook`, `src/agents/planner.py::Planner.plan`
   - language model: yes, `WorkflowCoordinator._plan` -> `Planner.plan`
   - reads: none
   - writes: `strategy.json`
3. **The model server checks and builds the design before anyone reads it; a refusal goes back to the Planner**
   - code: `workflow.py::WorkflowCoordinator._review_ready`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager.preview_design`
   - language model: yes, `WorkflowCoordinator._review_ready` -> `WorkflowCoordinator._plan` -> `Planner.plan`
   - MCP tools named: `build_domain_runs`, `check_domain_experiment`, `check_domain_inputs`, `describe_domain_controls`, `read_domain_recipe`, `write_domain_case`
   - reads: `domain_chain.json`, `domain_control_facts.json`, `domain_expectations.json`, `domain_recipe.json`, `inputs_check.json`
   - writes: `control_recipe.json`, `design_preview.json`, `domain_control_facts.json`, `domain_experiment.json`, `domain_recipe.json`, `source_changes.patch`, `strategy.json`, `strategy.refused_*.json`
4. **The design review page, and the person's decision**
   - code: `src/agents/design_review.py::write_review`, `src/agents/design_review.py::record_decision`
   - language model: no; code only
   - reads: `DESIGN_REVIEW.md`, `design_preview.json`, `reception.json`, `strategy.json`
   - writes: `DESIGN_REVIEW.md`
5. **The experiment record: control, runs and their checked changes**
   - code: `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._build_domain_experiment`
   - language model: no; code only
   - MCP tools named: `build_domain_runs`, `check_domain_experiment`, `check_domain_inputs`, `describe_domain_controls`, `read_domain_recipe`
   - reads: `domain_recipe.json`
   - writes: `domain_control_facts.json`, `domain_experiment.json`, `domain_recipe.json`
6. **Submit each run as a chain of scheduler jobs, with job B behind them**
   - code: `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._submit_experiment`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._submit_job_b`
   - language model: no; code only
   - MCP tools named: `submit_domain_chain`
   - reads: `chain.json`
   - writes: none
7. **Follow the chains and collect what each run produced**
   - code: `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._poll_experiment`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._collect_experiment`
   - language model: no; code only
   - MCP tools named: `check_domain_chain`
   - reads: `chain.json`
   - writes: `execution_report.txt`
8. **Extract each run's year numbers, and the regional numbers computed by the server's code (job B)**
   - code: `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._extract_experiment`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._regional`, `mcp/elm-mcp/src/domain_analysis.py::experiment`
   - language model: no; code only
   - reads: `chain.json`, `domain_control_facts.json`, `domain_experiment.json`, `strategy.json`
   - writes: `extracted.json`, `regional.json`
9. **Package the experiment record (job B)**
   - code: `mcp/elm-mcp/src/elm_exp_manager.py::ELMExpManager._package_experiment`
   - language model: no; code only
   - reads: `chain.json`, `domain_control_facts.json`, `domain_expectations.json`, `domain_recipe.json`, `regional.json`
   - writes: `experiment.json`
10. **The numbers report, rendered from the records (job B)**
   - code: `src/agents/analysis/domain_report.py::build`
   - language model: no; code only
   - reads: `experiment.json`, `reception.json`, `regional.json`, `strategy.json`
   - writes: `DOMAIN_REPORT.md`, `domain_report.json`
11. **Analyzer step 0: read the records into one context (job B)**
   - code: `src/agents/analysis/step0_context.py::load`
   - language model: no; code only
   - reads: `experiment.json`, `reception.json`, `strategy.json`
   - writes: none
12. **Analyzer steps 2 and 3: investigate, interpret, audit the claims (job B)**
   - code: `src/agents/analysis/step3_interpret.py::investigate_and_interpret`, `src/agents/analysis/step3_interpret.py::audit`
   - language model: yes, `investigate_and_interpret` -> `interpret`
   - reads: none
   - writes: `*_round*_*.txt`, `interpretation.json`, `investigation.json`, `investigation_plan.md`
13. **Analyzer step 4: the report (job B)**
   - code: `src/agents/analysis/step4_report.py::build`, `src/agents/analysis/step4_report.py::write`
   - language model: no; code only
   - reads: `DOMAIN_REPORT.md`, `RUN_SUMMARY.json`, `experiment.json`, `run_state.json`, `run_summary.json`
   - writes: `REPORT.md`, `analysis.json`
